games.note: P0 casts 2x Lotus Petal (turns 1-2), then Aether Vial ({1}) with payment_mode AutoExceptSacrificialMana. Engine offers ManaSourceSelection with 2 options (one per petal). Driver answers option 0, then answers the deferred ChooseManaColor with White. Petal sacrificed, vial resolves.

assertion_details.A4_ui_drops_color_detail: renders source name=True, renders 'sacrifice' caption=True, renders any color=False -> options visually indistinguishable: True
assertion_details.A5_selection_works_detail: answered=True chosen_color=Colorless cmc_answered=True cmc_chosen=White petal_sacrificed=True vial_on_bf=True

notes: Engine-level data is complete: each ManaSourceSelection option carries source_object_id, ability_index, mana_type, output (DeferredColorChoice for 'any color'), and penalty. The viewer_interaction projection ALSO carries a mana surface with symbols per choice (mss_viewer_interaction.json).

The shipped client's ManaSourceSelectionUI (ManaPaymentUI.tsx L627-690) reads waitingFor.data.options and renders each row as source-name + the translated 'sacrifice' caption only (L664-665). It never reads selection.mana_type, selection.output, or the interaction's mana surfaces, so every option from a multi-color sacrificial source renders identically: no color, no amount.
With 2 Lotus Petals the modal shows 2 identical rows ('Lotus Petal' / 'sacrifice'); the reporter can only process-of-elimination it. This is exactly the reported outcome.
A separate ChooseManaColor modal (shown after the source is picked) does render colors; it is not the broken path.
payment_mode AutoExceptSacrificialMana is a real client path: the shipped client's spell-payment preference stamps the same mode onto every cast (client/src/game/castPaymentMode.ts).
